user.title: MAST water meter
user.description: Paste the current `jwt` token from the MAST web app: log in at mast.co.il, open browser DevTools → Network, click any request to `api.mast.co.il` and copy the `jwt` request header. The token is valid for about 48 hours. You can automate this later with the userscript (see the README).

card.title: Choose your water card
card.description: Pick the water meter card to import. If your cards could not be listed automatically, type the card number.

webhook.title: Token push URL (optional)
webhook.description:
To send fresh tokens to Home Assistant automatically, install the userscript from the README and give it one of these URLs. Treat the URL as a secret: anyone who has it can push a token (it is only accepted if it works for your card).

Same network as Home Assistant:
`{internal_url}`

From anywhere:
`{external_url}`

You can show these again later via the integration's menu → Reconfigure.

reconfigure.title: Token push URL
reconfigure.description:
Give one of these URLs to the userscript. Treat it as a secret.

Same network as Home Assistant:
`{internal_url}`

From anywhere:
`{external_url}`

reauth_confirm.title: MAST token expired
reauth_confirm.description: Paste a fresh `jwt` token from the MAST web app, or just log in at mast.co.il in a browser with the userscript installed and this will resolve itself.

error.invalid_token: That does not look like a JWT token.
error.token_expired: That token has already expired. Copy a fresh one.
error.invalid_card: MAST returned an error. Check the card number.
error.no_data: The request worked but returned no readings.

abort.already_configured: This water card is already configured.
